items.claim: The statement that 19:15 restates the coming ruin rather than repeating the jar-oracle's own wording is byte-false, the cohesion binding 19:15 back across this unit's own opening seam goes undisclosed, and the setumah cited at 19:14 is in fact a break dividing the two verses of the span.
items.evidence: Confirmed: the quoted Hebrew reaches byte tier at its cited verses, the scene shift at 19:14 is byte-true (Topheth to the temple court, address to kol ha-am), and a petuchah after 19:13 corroborates the opening edge. Three defects. (1) The full title stack quoted at 19:15, יְהוָ֤ה צְבָאוֹת֙ אֱלֹהֵ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל, is byte-identical to the stack standing inside the jar-oracle at 19:3, two adjacent members of a 32-verse book-wide object (sweep: 32 verses); 19:15 then continues הִנְנִ֨י מבי מֵבִ֜יא against 19:3's הִנְנִ֨י מֵבִ֤יא רָעָה֙ עַל, the same hinneni-plus-participle construction over the same ra'ah object, and its own clause naming the evil already spoken points back into that earlier oracle. Both witnesses show it: “Behold, I will bring evil on this place” (web:Jer.19.3) beside the parallel announcement at web:Jer.19.15. So the non-repetition statement is contested by the bytes, and the device the unit cites as its own opening evidence is the same device that ties the two ends of the ch-19 complex together across the seam drawn at 19:13|19:14 - cohesion that goes undisclosed in the unit. (2) The ketiv/qere at 19:15 (inventory: 1 note) is the pair inside that same run, unpointed ketiv followed by pointed qere. The declared false-positive disposition is CONFIRMED on its narrow arm, since neither the quoted Hebrew nor the quoted English reaches that word; on the substantive arm it is REFUTED: the intervening ketiv token breaks the construction, so a contiguous consonantal sweep of hinneni-plus-participle returns 7 verses (5:15, 11:11, 19:3, 31:8, 35:17, 45:5, 49:5) and does not reach 19:15 - the one verse on which the non-repetition statement had to be tested. (3) The setumah cited as belonging to the span's opening verse is a break AFTER 19:14, dividing this two-verse span between its two verses; the spans at 20:1-20:6, 20:7-20:18, 21:1-21:7 and 22:1-22:9 say 'within the span' for that same configuration, and here the internal force is left unstated. The cut at 19:13|19:14 itself stands; the grounds offered for it do not.

items.claim: The rejected alternative tests a weaker internal rival than this unit's own disclosed evidence supports, and the byte-true renaming catchword straddling the closing seam at 20:6|20:7 goes undisclosed.
items.evidence: Confirmed: both quoted runs reach byte tier; the parashah citations are exact (no mark on 19:15, petuchah after 20:3, setumah after 20:6); the ketiv/qere inventory records nothing in 20:1-20:6; and the name-collision trap is passed - the patronymic is read as ben Immer at 20:1, distinct from the ben Malchiah of 21:1. Two defects. (1) The alternative weighed is a split at the day-change, i.e. 20:2|20:3, but the disclosed petuchah falls after 20:3 and 20:4 opens verse-initially on כִּ֣י כֹ֣ה אָמַ֣ר יְהוָ֡ה, a ki-subordinated koh-amar restart. Substrate break and frame restart coincide at 20:3|20:4, identifying a stronger internal rival that the field leaves untested, while the rival it does test carries neither signal. (2) The renaming said to bind 20:3-20:6 to a single act is מָג֥וֹר מִסָּבִֽיב, and the byte-identical run recurs outside this span at 20:10 as מָג֣וֹר מִסָּבִיב֒ within a 5-verse book-wide object (sweep: 5 verses: 6:25, 20:3, 20:10, 46:5, 49:29), with a third member of the object inside the span at 20:4 (לְמָג֜וֹר). Two of those five sit on either side of the seam this unit closes at, and a byte-true device straddling a unit's own seam argues continuity against the cut unless disclosed. Neither defect overturns the span, which the default of keeping an embedded oracle with its narrative frame supports.

items.claim: The stated ground for declining the split at 20:13|20:14 is contradicted by the bytes of 20:13 itself, and the digit offered for the confession cycle is put in sweep shorthand for a set no sweep produces.
items.evidence: Confirmed: both quoted runs reach byte tier, the turn to first-person address at 20:7 is byte-true, the ketiv/qere inventory records nothing in 20:7-20:18, and the parashah citations are exact (setumah after 20:6, after 20:12 and after 20:13; petuchah after 20:18). Three defects. (1) The rejected alternative rests on there being no discourse-frame imperative, addressee change or scene shift at the pivot. 20:13 reads שִׁ֚ירוּ לַֽיהוָ֔ה הַֽלְל֖וּ אֶת יְהוָ֑ה - two plural imperatives taking YHWH as their object, followed by a third-person ground clause - against 20:12's direct second-person address to YHWH (eleikha gilliti et rivi) and 20:14's addressee-less curse; both witnesses show it, “Sing to Yahweh! Praise Yahweh” (web:Jer.20.13). An imperative pair and an addressee change therefore stand at the declined pivot, and the setumah this unit itself discloses closes after 20:13, at that same point. The frontier flag and the held-open statement mitigate the boundary risk but do not repair a ground that the pivot verse's bytes contradict; a hymnic call to praise is also folded into a span typed as confession without a bytes-based type-deviation note. (2) '(sweep: 5 spans book-wide)' puts an editorially enumerated set into the sanctioned sweep shorthand: sweeps over this corpus return verse or token counts, not 'spans', and confession delimitation is not a byte-swept object - the enumeration is standard, its provenance misstated. (3) The taunt cited at 20:10 is מָג֣וֹר מִסָּבִיב֒, byte-identical to the renaming at 20:3 and part of a 5-verse book-wide object (sweep: 5 verses), straddling this unit's own opening seam at 20:6|20:7 undisclosed.

items.claim: The header at 21:1 is called dated although its temporal element is an occasion clause and 21:1 stands outside the classified date census (sweep: 19 candidate sites), and the addressee assigned to the 21:4-21:7 answer is not the one the bytes name.
items.evidence: Confirmed, and it matters at this frame seam: 21:1 opens verse-initially on אֲשֶׁר הָיָ֥ה אֶֽל יִרְמְיָ֖הוּ with the EL form spelled aleph-lamed, a genuine member of the eleven-verse ha-davar asher hayah el-Yirmeyahu shape and not the one-site ayin-lamed AL-variant header at 25:1, so the parent flip at exactly this verse is byte-warranted; the petuchah after 20:18 corroborates it, the setumah after 21:2 is correctly reported as within the span, the patronymic ben Malchiah is quoted so the 20:1 name collision is passed, and the koh-amar at 21:4 is quoted without tsevaot rather than blended into the fuller title stack. Two defects. (1) 'A dated royal embassy' is byte-false: the temporal element in 21:1 is בִּשְׁלֹ֨חַ אֵלָ֜יו הַמֶּ֣לֶךְ צִדְקִיָּ֗הוּ, a bet-prefixed infinitive construct naming an occasion, lacking a year word and lacking the bet-plus-cardinal shape, and 21:1 sits outside the classified date census (sweep: 19 candidate sites book-wide). The filed signal list omits any date entry, and the WEB header quoted at web:Jer.21.1 shows no date either, so the prose overshoots both its own signals and both witnesses. (2) The relay verse 21:3 reads כֹּ֥ה תֹאמְרֻ֖ן אֶל צִדְקִיָּֽהוּ - thus you shall say to Zedekiah - naming Zedekiah as addressee, and the oracle body then speaks in the plural to those holding the weapons (21:4 be-yedkhem, attem nilchamim, ha-tsarim aleikhem). The rejected alternative's warrant, that 21:8 shifts the address from the king's own messengers to the people at large, therefore mis-names the prior addressee: the messengers are couriers, not the addressee. The seam at 21:7|21:8 survives; the warrant stated for it does not describe the bytes.

items.claim: The addressee the seam warrant turns on is mis-named, the English gloss drops the formula its own Hebrew run carries, and an unflagged ketiv/qere sits on the surrender clause this unit argues from.
items.evidence: Confirmed: both quoted runs reach byte tier, the commission at 21:8 is verse-initial, the shift of address to ha-am ha-zeh is byte-true, and the parashah citations are exact (no mark on 21:7; setumah after 21:10 closing the span). Three defects. (1) The prior addressee is Zedekiah, named at 21:3 in כֹּ֥ה תֹאמְרֻ֖ן אֶל צִדְקִיָּֽהוּ, not the king's own messengers; the shift at 21:8 is real, but its point of departure is stated wrongly, and that point of departure is the seam warrant. (2) The quoted Hebrew run at 21:8 ends כֹּ֖ה אָמַ֣ר יְהוָ֑ה while the English gloss stops at the commission clause; the formula is rendered inside the same verse in the other witness (“Yahweh says”, web:Jer.21.8), so the parity gap is this unit's own cut and not the translation's, and the formula inside the filed koh-amar signal reaches the packet unglossed. (3) 21:9 carries a ketiv/qere (inventory: 1 note), the pair יחיה וְחָיָ֔ה - unpointed ketiv then pointed qere - standing on the verb that governs the surrender outcome this unit summarizes as the terms of surrender at 21:9. No disclosure appears in the unit, and the declared queue holds nothing here because no quote binds to that verse, so the variant is neither declared nor examined; a verse whose content is argued in prose owes the check before the argument.

items.claim: The declared closure signal is positionally false at both cited sites - neither neum-YHWH occurrence closes its verse and the span's closing verse does not end on the formula - and the ketiv/qere at 21:12 alternates precisely the addressee this unit's driver depends on.
items.evidence: Confirmed: the quoted runs reach byte tier, 21:11 really is the whole verse (six words), the vocative bet-david is verse-initial at 21:12, and the parashah citations are exact (setumah after 21:10 and after 21:14). Three defects. (1) The statement that the oracle closes on neum-YHWH twice does not hold positionally. At 21:13 the formula stands at word 7 of 15, running on into נְאֻם יְהוָ֑ה הָאֹֽמְרִים֙; at 21:14 it stands at word 5 of 12, running on into נְאֻם יְהוָ֑ה וְהִצַּ֤תִּי אֵשׁ֙, so the span's closing verse ends on the fire clause rather than on the formula. Through this span every occurrence is clause-internal - 21:7, 21:10, 21:13, 21:14 and 22:5, five of five mid-verse - and the formula corroborates closure where a fresh onset follows, which holds for 21:14 (the imperative-bearing koh-amar at 22:1 that this unit rightly cites) but not for 21:13. (2) 21:12 carries a ketiv/qere (inventory: 1 note): מעלליהם מַעַלְלֵיכֶֽם, third-person-plural ketiv against second-person-plural qere on the deeds. The declared false-positive disposition is CONFIRMED on the quote-binding arm - the quoted bet-david is verse-initial and the variant verse-final - but REFUTED on the substantive arm, because the driver filed for this unit is the addressee and the variant is an addressee alternation, with 21:14's unvaried כִּפְרִ֥י מַעַלְלֵיכֶ֖ם standing on the qere side of it. (3) The span's opening word is וּלְבֵית֙, vav-prefixed and lamed-topical, a conjunctive onset left unweighed against the fresh-address claim; and a koh-amar stands inside the span at 21:12 without appearing among the filed signals, unlike the neighbouring spans at 21:8-21:10 and 22:1-22:9.

items.claim: The ground stated for declining the split at 22:6 - no change of frame-owner or addressee - is contradicted by the bytes, by both witnesses and by this unit's own rationale sentence, at a juncture the parashah layer independently marks, and two ketiv/qere verses inside the span go undisclosed.
items.evidence: Confirmed: both quoted runs reach byte tier, the commission at 22:1 is verse-initial, and the parashah citations are exact (setumah after 21:14, after 22:2, after 22:5 and after 22:9). Three defects. (1) At 22:1 the house is the destination of a commission - רֵ֖ד בֵּֽית מֶ֣לֶךְ יְהוּדָ֑ה - and 22:2 addresses the king directly in the singular (shema dvar YHWH melekh Yehudah ... attah va-avadeikha). At 22:6 the same three-word phrase returns under a different preposition, עַל בֵּית֙ מֶ֣לֶךְ יְהוּדָ֔ה, ayin-lamed 'concerning', and the singular now addresses the house itself (gilad attah li; 22:7 mivchar arazeikha, your cedars). The phrase is a 7-verse book-wide object (sweep: 7 verses: 21:11, 22:1, 22:6, 27:18, 27:21, 32:2, 38:22), and this span carries two of them under two different frames. The shift shows in both witnesses - “Go down to the house of the king of Judah” (web:Jer.22.1) against “concerning the house of the king of Judah” (web:Jer.22.6) - so it is not translation-dependent. The rejected alternative's ground is therefore false as to addressee, and it contradicts this unit's own rationale, which states that the address turns from the reigning king to the house itself. (2) The setumah disclosed after 22:5 falls at exactly the 22:5|22:6 juncture the rejected alternative declines to cut; disclosed in one field, it is left unweighed in the other, so the weak corroboration that happens to point the same way as the bytes stays out of the reasoning it bears on. (3) Two ketiv/qere verses sit in the span (inventory: 1 note each at 22:4 and 22:6) and neither is disclosed. The 22:4 pair ועבדו וַעֲבָדָ֖יו - singular ketiv against plural qere on the retinue - sits inside the very promise clause this unit paraphrases and stands outside the declared flag queue, which is therefore incomplete here; the disposition on the 22:6 warn is CONFIRMED on its narrow arm, since the quoted English stops well before the verse-final variant.

items.claim: A verse-initial koh-amar frame inside the span is left out of the filed signals, the setumah that divides the span is reported without its internal force, and the type-guess supplies an identification the bytes do not carry.
items.evidence: Confirmed, and the closing edge is the best-supported seam in this cluster: both quoted runs reach byte tier, the negative imperatives are verse-initial at 22:10, the ketiv/qere inventory records nothing in 22:10-22:12, the parashah citations are factually right (setumah after 22:9, after 22:10 and after 22:12), and the break after 22:12 is immediately followed by the verse-initial woe onset at 22:13, one of the two woe-oracle onsets in the role-split hoy inventory. Three defects, and the span stands under them. (1) 22:11 opens on כִּ֣י כֹ֣ה אָֽמַר יְ֠הוָה, a verse-initial ki-subordinated koh-amar, which the filed signals omit although the same shape is filed for the spans at 20:1-20:6, 21:1-21:7, 21:8-21:10 and 22:1-22:9; the ki does subordinate, so cohesion holds and the cut is not in doubt, but the frame device goes undisclosed in a unit whose seam argument is about onsets. (2) The setumah at 22:10 is a break AFTER 22:10 and therefore divides this three-verse span between 22:10 and 22:11-22:12; it is reported as a mark on the span's opening verse, with that internal force left unstated. (3) The Hebrew run quoted from 22:11 stops at the royal title while the English gloss runs on through ha-molekh tachat Yoshiyahu aviv, a gloss longer than its run; and the type-guess reads the unnamed dead of 22:10 as Josiah, which 22:10-22:12 do not state - Josiah appears there as Shallum's father.
